full_judgment: 5. The learned Advocate further submits that the condition precedent for taking away the right of exemption of the petitioner from payment of VAT and Income Tax is a notification in the official gazette and since there is no such notification published in the official gazette requiring the petitioner to pay VAT and income tax the purported exercise of power of the respondent.1 and 2 is illegal, arbitrary and therefore the same is without lawful authority. He further contended that none of the provisions of the Income Tax Act, Business Profit Tax (Amendment) Act 1949, the Income Tax(Amendment) Act.1950 and the Income tax Ordinance 1984 and the Pakistan Finance Act (Amendment) Ordinance 1949 shall apply to the indigenous Hillman and as such imposition of Income Tax on the petitioner by the respondents No.1 and 2 is illegal, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Mr. Islam then contended that the impugned order is also discriminatory inasmuch as the Government has given exemption from payment of VAT to 12 (twelve) Cinema Halls within the Chittagong Hill Tracts by Notification dated 12.7.93 but inspite of that the authority have levied VAT and Income Tax upon the imported goods of the petitioner. Mr. Islam then relying on Article 28(4) of the Constitution submitted that the said Article provides for making special provision to promulgate any law for the improvement of backward section of citizen and also in favour of women or children or for the advancement of any backward section of citizen of Bangladesh. Mr. Islam very emphatically submits that the provisions of VAT Act have no manner of application in the said Districts in as much as in the Act itself there is no mention that the Act will be applicable through out Bangladesh. Therefore, since the provision is in conflict with the Regulation, in as much as the Act has not been notified in pursuance of the provision of Article 4(2) of the Regulation, the provision of Regulation shall prevail over the Act. He further submits that the admitted position is that the exemption of the Income Tax has been extended to the Indigenous Hillman though the said Act has been applied within the area of Chittagong Hill Tracts, therefore since the company has been floated by the people living within the territorial District of Khagrachari is entitled to get the benefit of the Regulation which is still a good law. It is also contended by Mr. Islam that the benefit extended by the Regulation has been enjoyed by the Hill Tracts people for generations and that benefit cannot now be withdrawn arbitrarily without notifying the enactment in question in Gazette under Article 4(2) of the Regulation to include the same in the schedule of the Regulation. Mr. Islam submitted that his submissions also get support from the summary (Annexure-D) which has been placed before the Prime Minister for extending the area of operation of VAT Act to the Hill Districts. Therefore there is no doubt that the Regulation is still in force and effective.
